contract_plain_english: If p and u solve the one-dimensional acoustics system, then w^1 = p + rho c u, with c = sqrt(K/rho), satisfies w^1_t + c w^1_x = 0. Thus this characteristic variable is transported at the positive sound speed +c and represents the right-going acoustic wave.

binders: w^1(x,t) = p(x,t) + rho c u(x,t), the right-going characteristic variable
conclusions: The combination w^1 = p + rho c u satisfies w^1_t + c w^1_x = 0.
This scalar equation has propagation velocity +c and hence describes the right-going acoustic mode.
definitions_and_conventions: The superscript 1 labels the first characteristic variable; it is not an exponent.
Under the source's scalar advection convention v_t + a v_x = 0, the coefficient +c is the signed velocity.
The terminology right-going uses c > 0 and the usual orientation of the x-axis.
hypotheses: p and u satisfy p_t + K u_x = 0 and u_t + (1/rho) p_x = 0.
The fields have the differentiability needed for the displayed first derivatives.
K and rho are the positive constant physical parameters, so c is a positive constant and rho is nonzero.
implicit_context: The identity follows by differentiating the defined linear combination and substituting both equations in (1.5), together with c^2 = K/rho.
The positivity and regularity conditions are understood from the physical and differential-equation context rather than separately displayed.
Although the neighboring discussion gives a translated-profile formula explicitly for the second mode, the first-mode claim on this page is the displayed transport equation itself.

details: The coefficient of u is exactly +rho c.
Both equations of the acoustics system contribute to the transport identity.
The PDE sign is w^1_t + c w^1_x = 0.
Its signed propagation velocity is +c, the right-going sound speed.

undebatable_constraints: Define the mode exactly as p + rho c u.
Retain c = sqrt(K/rho) with the positive physical sound-speed convention.
Conclude w^1_t + c w^1_x = 0 with the plus sign.
Preserve the interpretation as the +c, right-going acoustic mode.
